rows.why: How training, tuning and evaluation data are collected and selected (availability, representativeness, suitability) and how the test harness is designed is identified and documented.
The sources of training, tuning and test data, including third-party and public datasets and reused feedback, are inventoried with the licence or other right to use each for training.

Controls protecting datasets and the evaluation harness from poisoning and tampering (access, separation of who curates data from who trains, isolation, encryption) are identified and documented, including for third-party data.
Evaluation sets and the harness are held or reviewed by people independent of the developers, so they cannot be changed to hide failures.
The test sets, metrics and harness tools used to evaluate the model are documented and versioned, so a result can be traced to the exact data and test cases used.
Datasets built from people's data are collected with consent and human-subject protections and are checked to be representative of the population the model will serve.
The evaluation and test sets are checked to reflect the conditions the model will be deployed in, including non-optimised and edge cases, not only clean or convenient data.
The harness and evaluation sets are checked to be valid, so the test cases measure what they claim and results are not inflated by overlap with the training data.
Training, tuning and evaluation data are tested for poisoning, injected records and tampering before use, and the results are documented.
Changes to training, tuning and evaluation datasets and to the harness are logged with who made them and when, so tampering can be traced and accounted for.
Personal and sensitive data in training sets and in feedback or logs reused for tuning is found, minimised or removed, and access to it is controlled.
The evaluation sets and harness are reviewed to confirm they still catch known failures and have not been weakened or become stale.

When poisoned, tampered or unlawfully used data is discovered, the models trained or evaluated on it are identified, the data is restored from a clean copy, and the incident is recorded, reported to the owners of the affected models and reviewed.
Third-party and public datasets and benchmarks are monitored for licence changes, withdrawals and reported contamination, and the risk controls applied are documented.
Deletion and rectification requests are tracked through to the training, tuning and evaluation datasets and reused feedback that hold the affected data.
User feedback and logs are vetted for quality, sensitive data and manipulation before they are reused to tune or update the model.

review.reason: also_covers still names MANAGE 4.3, but the why reports the incident only to the owners of the affected models; it does not tell the users of those models or the people whose data was unlawfully used (affected communities), which the round-1 finding asked for.

Dropped from MANAGE 2.3's also_covers and now unmapped: nothing checks that a poisoned or unlawfully used dataset can be pulled from training and evaluation pipelines and that models trained or evaluated on it are stopped or replaced.
